From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Embeddings fit validation — follow-up + recommended next steps

Hi Susan,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to hear more about Acme's search use case (catalog search + support docs). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear mutual action plan: 

1) Goals (from our conversation)
- Improve semantic search relevance for product catalog and KB articles.
- Reduce false positives on short queries and improve recall for long-tail SKUs.
- Maintain latency SLOs (search < 50ms tokenization + vector lookup) and keep storage/cost reasonable.

2) Recommended quick evaluation (what we can run as a pilot)
- Dataset: your sample 5k doc bundle (product descriptions + 500 labeled query->relevant doc pairs).
- Models to compare: a) 1536-d managed embedding (Redwood-emb-1536-v2) for best quality, b) 512-d compressed variant (Redwood-emb-512-proj) for cost/latency tradeoff.
- Metrics: MRR, recall@10, nDCG@10, average cosine distance for positives vs negatives, and drift check (cosine distribution shift).
- Indexing: FAISS IVF+PQ baseline (IVF512, PQ16) and a small HNSW config for low-latency testing.

3) Known risks / quality regression concerns
- If you reindex frequently without re-evaluating, changes to the encoder (retraining/updates) can shift embeddings and degrade production relevance. We'll provide a lightweight regression test (your labeled set) to gate any updates.

4) Data & timeline
- Please share the sample bundle and the labeled pairs (or give us read access to the Drive link). If we get the data by EOD Tuesday we can run the 1st-pass evaluation in ~7 business days and deliver a results deck + recommended config.

Attached: prompt_set.csv (examples we plan to use for prompt-based retrieval), baseline_benchmarks.pdf (our prior retail catalog baseline), and a one-page mutual_action_plan.docx.

Next call: I'll book a 30-min sync to review the results and propose a pilot scope. Does Wednesday 8/18 at 10am PT work?

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,

Subject: Re: Embeddings fit validation — model recommendations (internal)

Internal notes / recommendation: 
- Run both: Redwood-emb-1536-v2 (best quality) and Redwood-emb-512-proj. For production we usually prefer 1536 for catalog-heavy semantics. 512 is useful for latency/cost-constrained endpoints and often fine with a re-ranker.
- Include int8 quantized pass on the 1536 only to measure quality drop; I expect <1.5% MRR delta in many retail datasets but depends on long-tail SKUs.
- Evaluation config: 5k corpus, 500 labeled queries. Metrics: MRR, recall@1/5/10, nDCG@10, mean cosine positive vs negative, A/B slow-query percentile (p95 latency).
- Drift check: compute cosine distribution on a rolling time window and flag when mean shift >0.05 and sigma changes >0.02 — we'll include a small dashboard.
- Index suggestions: FAISS IVF512,PQ16 baseline; HNSW with efConstruction=200 for low-latency tests. For production consider hybrid retriever+cross-encoder re-ranker for top-20.

Link to prior retail benchmark: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RetailBenchmarkExample (see table 2 for embedding dim comparisons).

I'll draft the test harness artifacts (scripts + result templates) and push to the shared folder by EOD.

—Marcus
